Topic1.Title: Bike Security and Theft Reduction Update
Topic1.Summary: Staff from Transportation and Mobility and the Boulder Police Department presented completed work on the council priority to reduce bike theft and improve bike security. Bike theft fell 14% year-over-year in 2026 and recovery rose 13%, with the team expecting to meet its 10% goals. Actions included Bike Index registration events, locking education, bike rack upgrades, and targeted bait-bike operations. Council members asked about data gaps, staffing constraints, e-bike theft, and encouraging bike shops to register bikes at sale. Remaining tasks include a long-term bike parking resource and downtown station signage.

Topic2.Title: Enhancing Boulder's Wildfire Resilience
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the Wildfire Ready 2030 framework, organized into four strategies and 25 programs with 10 tier-one priorities, supported by a Wildland Urban Interface Risk Index that ranks 12 western sections. They also introduced a Wildfire Ready Action Hub for residents, 14 performance measures, and roughly $10 million in current tier-one investment. Staff proposed about $1.85 million in 2027 enhancements from grants and an open space fund realignment. Council members pressed for more aggressive hardening targets, a mandatory hardening ordinance, contractor quality standards, evacuation and cell-coverage planning, and reconciling wildfire building standards.
